creation: AI-generated raster images using built-in image generation. Revised after user feedback toward muted, restrained pixel illustration. Not human-authored art.

atlases.prompt: Use case: style-transfer, game background atlas. Redraw the supplied four-panel atlas in a MUCH SIMPLER, restrained, human-crafted indie pixel-art aesthetic. Keep the 2x2 equal quadrant layout and the four narrative locations (night train platform, train compartment, maintenance engine room, river at dawn), but completely replace the rendering style. The previous polished decorative artwork was rejected as too AI-looking. Target: carefully placed coarse pixel clusters, like a small independent artist actually working on a 320x180 pixel canvas per scene. Limited palette of about 24 muted colors total, matte navy/slate/ochre/dusty pink, large areas of quiet flat color, only 2 or 3 shadow tones per object. Strong slightly imperfect silhouettes, deliberately simplified geometry, asymmetrical mundane details such as one crooked stool and a forgotten cup. Short dither patches only where needed; no speckled texture pasted everywhere. Korean suburban silver commuter train, practical interior, conductor with a plain cap, people tiny and understated. REMOVE excessive flowers, copper filigree, Victorian ornament, glitter, big glowing portals, dramatic fantasy bloom and decorative clutter. Engine room should have practical pipes and a small cyan signal lamp rather than a cosmic portal. Dawn is soft and subdued, not glowing epic golden sunrise. Hard pixel edges throughout, no smooth gradients, no photorealism, no 3D, no lens effects, no depth-of-field blur. Each wide scene must read as an intentional hand-composed pixel painting with negative space. No text, no logos, no captions, no borders. Four equal edge-to-edge quadrants, subjects entirely within their own quadrant. Desired mood: intimate, ordinary, a little lonely and weird; mature indie adventure game background.
